subject: Org health: decision lanes, QBR inputs, and cross-team blockers
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Org health: decision lanes, QBR inputs, and cross-team blockers

Team — quick morning brief ahead of the QBR pack deadline. I’m sending a concise status: wins, current risks, and explicit asks where I need decisions / help today. Deck attached (QBR deck + migration roadmap). Link to raw metrics in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QbrInputXYZ

Wins:
- Hosted API latency SLO met across north-south regions; median 92ms for 512-token paths (pipeline optimizations shipped last week).
- Two Dedicated renewals verbally confirmed (ACME & PayWise) — legal redlines in flight.

Risks / open issues:
1) Migration runway: internal infra team flags a 3-week potential delay if we don’t allocate two extra backend sprints to the KV cache refactor (see migration-roadmap-attach.xlsx). Impact: could push certain QBR throughput commitments into next quarter.
2) PayWise procurement is requesting a custom data-retention clause; legal needs a direct point to triage further (Procurement already involved).
3) Dashboard gating: Product analytics noted missing reconciliation for token billing parity vs usage logs — this blocks final cost slide accuracy.

Asks (urgent / require reply by EOD):
- Markus: confirm whether we can re-prioritize the infra sprint to cover cache refactor (yes/no) so I can lock the QBR commit. If yes, propose which two-week window.
- Maya: please validate the NPS + onboarding metrics for slide 6; I flagged two datapoints that looked inconsistent — advise corrected values or confirm current numbers.
- Grace / Jonas: I need a short blurb (1-2 bullets) on enterprise sales motions and expected renewal cadence for PayWise to include in the customer health slide.
- Evelyn: loop Legal + Procurement on the PayWise clause; add procurement@bigbank.com if they want to discuss precedent.

Attachment stubs: 2027-Q2-QBR-deck-laura.pdf (master), migration-roadmap-attach.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll consolidate replies and post an updated deck by 15:30 PT.

— Laura
Laura Bennett | VP, Strategy & Ops | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org health: decision lanes, QBR inputs, and cross-team blockers

Laura — thanks for the clear ask. Quick take:
- I approve re-prioritizing the next infra sprint to include the KV cache refactor. We can pull two engineers from non-customer-facing work and shift the sprint window to 2027-05-31 → 2027-06-13. That should cover the critical path for throughput parity.
- Caveat: this reduces capacity for one non-urgent performance spike task; I’ll notify the owner and get their alignment.

Action: I’ll add a short note to the decision lanes doc and queue the sprint change with PM. Laura, you can mark the migration risk as "managed" for the QBR if you’re comfortable with that timeline.

— Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Engineering | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org health: decision lanes, QBR inputs, and cross-team blockers

Laura / Markus — I reviewed the metrics and made two adjustments:
- Onboarding time (slide 6): corrected median day-1 activation from 2.8 → 2.4 days (we were pulling an outdated pre-optim).
- Net revenue retention shown on slide 8 should be 114.2% (not 111.7%). I’ll replace the source sheet in the Drive folder.

Note: the billing parity issue is a reconciliation edge-case — Finance will publish a final reconciled token map by tomorrow morning. If you need me to update the deck before 15:30 PT, I can, but I’ll wait for the finance note to avoid a second pass.

Attachment: small CSV with metric diffs uploaded to Drive.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan | Head of Product | Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai

From: Patricia Gomez <patricia@paywise.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bigbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Org health: decision lanes, QBR inputs, and cross-team blockers

Laura / Evelyn — appreciate the heads-up and the draft contract language you shared via DocuSign link earlier. Procurement here has one ask to simplify the retention clause to a 90-day default with an enterprise opt-in for longer retention. We’re okay moving quickly if Legal can provide a short redline and a precedent example.

Procurement contact: Juan Alvarez (juan.alvarez@bigbank.com) — they can jump on a short call tomorrow if needed.

Best,
Patricia Gomez
GM, Customer Success | PayWise
patricia@paywise.com
